identification.title: Great I Am
identification.notes: Written by Jared Anderson alone; copyright 2011 Integrity Worship Music, administered by Integrity Music; CCLI 5881491; original key D per PraiseCharts. Anderson led worship at New Life Church, Colorado Springs, and the song appears on the Great I Am EP credited to New Life Worship and Jared Anderson. The list's artist is right. Other-language versions credit extra adapters (Olmes Corrales, Sebastian Bartram), but the English original is Anderson's. Reviewed as the song, not as any one recording; live versions add spontaneous extension.

claims.structuralNotes: Two verses, a chorus repeated after each, and a bridge about the power of the Lord's name. The verses are in the first person singular and voice desires: to be close to God, to hear angels sing, to see dry bones live, to love the world and hate the dark; one line sets heaven's reality against death. The chorus addresses God directly as holy and almighty, the great I Am, and asks who is worthy, answering that none is beside him. The bridge is a third-person proclamation that mountains shake and demons flee at his name and that no power in hell can stand before his presence.

strengths.title: The I AM name in the chorus
strengths.explanation: The chorus rests on the divine name given to Moses and claimed by Christ, and joins it to God's holiness and almightiness, so the praise is grounded in who God is.
strengths.scriptureRationale: God's self-disclosure as I AM, the name the chorus takes up.

strengths.title: None beside him
strengths.explanation: The chorus asks who is worthy and answers that no one else is, which keeps the song from praising a mood and puts it on God alone.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Lamb alone worthy, with angels and the church answering.

strengths.title: Evil cannot stand before him
strengths.explanation: The bridge proclaims that nature and demons give way before God's name and that hell has no standing in his presence.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Every knee bowing at the name above every name.

doctrinesAffirmed: The holiness and almightiness of God
God as the great I Am
The authority of God's name over evil
theological.assessment: No concern kept. The verse line setting heaven's reality against death is a figure: death is a real enemy in Scripture, but an ordinary congregation hears the line as saying death does not have the last word, which 1 Corinthians 15 affirms, so it does not affirmatively teach that death is unreal. The wish to love the world while hating the dark echoes John 3:16 and Romans 12:9. The verses are the singer's own longing and the gospel is only implicit.

strengths.title: A chorus a room can sing at once
strengths.explanation: The chorus is short, simple in its progression, and builds, so a congregation picks it up on the first pass.

strengths.title: Suits gathering and adoration
strengths.explanation: Its focus on God's name and holiness fits a call to worship or a response after a reading.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Published with D as the original key per PraiseCharts. The chorus is easy; the bridge range is moderately wide and builds, so check it for a mixed congregation.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The chorus returns after each verse and the bridge repeats in a long build, and live versions extend it spontaneously, so the repetition does more of the work than the few lines of words.
communal.assessment: The chorus is congregational and easy. The bridge is a high-energy build that leans on repetition and can move toward the leader's performance if extended. Kept to the written form it serves a room well.

strengths.title: The addressee is named by the divine name
strengths.explanation: The chorus calls God the great I Am, holy and almighty, so the song is plainly about the LORD and not an unnamed you.

clarity.assessment: The chorus and bridge are clear. The verses are the singer's longings and one line about death is figurative and can be heard more than one way, though the usual hearing is orthodox. The song never states the gospel, so its work is adoration.

synthesis.summary: A song of adoration built on the divine name: verses voice the singer's longing for God's presence, heaven and revival, the chorus addresses God as holy, almighty and the great I Am with none beside him, and the bridge proclaims evil's powerlessness before his presence. One verse line on death is figurative. No concerns kept; the gospel is not stated. No independent source assessing its content was found.

scriptureReferences.relevance: The divine name I AM, taken up in the chorus.
Christ claiming the name before Abraham was.
The thrice-holy God of the chorus.
The question of who is worthy, answered in the Lamb.
Dry bones living - the second verse's longing.
Death as the last enemy, defeated by Christ.
